articles.title: MLB Wild Card Series 2026 Calendar: Dates and teams for every game in the first round of the postseason
articles.standfirst: The New York Yankees will take on the Boston Red Sox in the American League bracket.
articles.summary: The New York Yankees will take on the Boston Red Sox in the American League bracket.
articles.body:
The 2026 MLB postseason is almost here, with four best-of-three Wild Card Series beginning September 29 and several matchups already set for the opening round of October. Even though the regular season is entering its final weekend, but much of the postseason picture is already clear as ten teams have secured playoff spots – but key seeds and division races remain unresolved.

The Tampa Bay Rays have secured the Americal League 's No. 1 seed, while the Milwaukee Brewers own the MLB 's best record and will enter October as the National League 's top seed. The Los Angeles Dodgers , New York Yankees , Atlanta Braves , Boston Red Sox , Chicago Cubs , Chicago White Sox , Cleveland Guardians and San Diego Padres have also secured postseason berths. Heading into the final day, the Philadelphia Phillies are still battling for position in the National League, while the Houston Astros and Texas Rangers remain locked in the race for the AL West pennant. And the first confirmed Wild Card matchup features one of baseball's most recognizable rivalries, with the Red Sox and Yankees set to meet in a best-of-three series. The series begins Tuesday, September 29, at Yankee Stadium , with Game 2 scheduled for Wednesday, September 30. A decisive Game 3 will be played Thursday, October 1, if necessary. The two teams have played 13 times during the regular season, with New York narrowly winning the series 7-6. The Yankees also went 4-2 against Boston at home. The rivalry returns to the postseason after the Yankees defeated Boston 2-1 in the 2025 AL Wild Card Series before advancing to the AL Division Series . Aaron Judge is also expected to be a major storyline after indicating that he wants to return for October, but he is facing a race against time if he aims to get back onto the field for New York . Meanwhile Boston will turn to rookie left-hander Payton Tolle , who posted a 3.03 ERA during his debut season. Tolle recorded a 0.69 ERA with 18 strikeouts across 13 innings against New York .

2026 MLB Wild Card Series schedule

The other Wild Card matchups will be determined by the final standings, with the remaining division and playoff races still capable of changing the opening-round bracket. The 2026 MLB postseason will eventually build toward the World Series , with the Wild Card round providing the first opportunity for teams to begin their October championship run. Below is the schedule you need to follow: Tuesday, September 29 – Game 1 AL Wild Card Series A Game 1 AL Wild Card Series B, Game 1 NL Wild Card Series A, Game 1 NL Wild Card Series B, Game 1 Wednesday, September 30 AL Wild Card Series A, Game 2 AL Wild Card Series B, Game 2 NL Wild Card Series A, Game 2 NL Wild Card Series B, Game 2 Thursday, October 1 (Game 3 will only be played if necessary) AL Wild Card Series A, Game 3 AL Wild Card Series B, Game 3 NL Wild Card Series A, Game 3 NL Wild Card Series B, Game 3

articles.title: MLB Wild Card Series 2026 odds: Which team is more likely to make it to the Divisional Round?
articles.standfirst: Can the New York Yankees defeat the Boston Red Sox?
articles.summary: Can the New York Yankees defeat the Boston Red Sox?
articles.body:
The 2026 MLB postseason begins Tuesday with four best-of-three Wild Card Series , putting eight teams within two wins of the Divisional Series , but how do the matchups compare entering October? The road to the World Series begins with four Wild Card clashes, each featuring a best-of-three format. The higher seed hosts all three potential games, giving the New York Yankees , Houston Astros, Atlanta Braves and San Diego Padres home-field advantage against their respective opponents.

The Yankees face the Red Sox in the American League , with New York holding the stronger position at a 60.2% probability of reaching the AL Divisional Round , whilst Boston has a 39.8% chance of advancing. The Red Sox finished the regular season strongly and have the pitching depth to make the series competitive, but the Yankees ' home-field advantage gives them the higher projected chance - especially if Aaron Judge returns. Meanwhile, the Astros and White Sox have one of the closest projected match-ups but Chicago are at a disadvantage, given a 42.9% chance of moving on, compared with 57.1% for Houston . The White Sox enter with an 84-78 record and an offense capable of producing in a short series. Houston finished 81-81 with one of the worst modern records to win a division, but captured the AL West pennant , with Yordan Alvarez providing a major threat.

The Braves have the best chance in the National League

The Braves have one of largest projected advantages among the four Wild Card matchups as Atlanta is given a 53.3% chance of eliminating the Phillies , compared with 46.7% for Philadelphia . The Braves finished 94-68 and enter with a division title, home-field advantage and Chris Sale anchoring the pitching staff. Their lineup also provides significant power, making Atlanta a difficult opponent in a short series. Philadelphia , however, has the frontline pitching to challenge Atlanta . Zack Wheeler , Cristopher Sanchez and Jesus Luzardo give the visitors multiple options capable of changing a series with one dominant outing. The Padres have a 52.1% chance of advancing against the Cubs , who sit at 47.9% as San Diego finished 91-71 and brings a deep bullpen and star power led by Fernando Tatis Jr. and Jackson Merrill . Chicago went 89-73 but needs to improve its pitching. Across the four matchups, the projections point to the Yankees and Astros having the clearest statistical edge, while the Braves-Phillies and Cubs-Padres series are almost essentially toss-ups. Awaiting the winners of the Wild Card games are the Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians in the American League , whilst the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers are already in the National League Divisional Series .

articles.title: MLB Wild Card Series Format: How many games are played in this round and which teams qualified for the 2026 postseason?
articles.standfirst: Eight teams fight for four tickets to the Division Series in an intense Wild Card round
articles.summary: Eight teams fight for four tickets to the Division Series in an intense Wild Card round
articles.body:
The excitement of the 2026 MLB postseason is already underway, with the Wild Card Series kicking off this Tuesday September 29. The format once again relies on the intensity of short series, with only three games per matchup and each one crucial to the teams' aspirations.

This year, there will be four matchups, two per league, to determine the teams that advance to the Divisional Round. With historic rivalries, maximum excitement and teams with no margin for error, the road to the 2025 World Series begins

How does the 2026 MLB Wild Card work and how many games are played?

The Wild Card round maintains its format established in recent seasons: best-of-three series and the higher-seeded team in each series is the host throughout the tie, which could make the difference in such close games.

The Tampa Bay Rays, Cleveland Guardians, Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers were the four teams that earned an initial bye, advancing directly to the next phase for finishing among the best in their respective leagues. Meanwhile, the other eight teams face off this week in a schedule that could change the course of the postseason.

Which teams qualified for the 2026 MLB Wild Card and When are the matchups?

In the American League, the spotlight is on high-voltage duels: Chicago White Sox at Houston Astros and Boston Red Sox at New York Yankees. In both cases, there are divisional rivalries at play, which further raises the tension. The schedule for this games will be:

Chicago White Sox at Houston Astros

Game 1 : Tuesday September 29, at 5:00 p.m. ET

Game 2 : Wednesday September 30, at 5:00 p.m. ET

Game 3 : Thursday October 1, TBD*

Boston Red Sox at New York Yankees

Game 1 : Tuesday September 29, at 8:00 p.m. ET

Game 2 : Wednesday September 30, at 8:00 p.m. ET

The winner of each matchup will advance to the Divisional Round, where the teams that received a bye are already waiting. From there, the series will be best-of-five and then, both the Championship Series and World Series will be best-of-seven.

articles.title: MLB Playoffs 2026 Prize Money: How much are players making per round during postseason?
articles.standfirst: Postseason payouts rise sharply from the Wild Card round to the World Series
articles.summary: Postseason payouts rise sharply from the Wild Card round to the World Series
articles.body:
The deeper a Major League Baseball team advances in the postseason, the more valuable October becomes for the players involved.

MLB doesn't simply hand out a fixed bonus after each round. Instead, postseason teams split a central players’ pool funded largely by ticket revenue from designated playoff games, with the largest percentage reserved for the eventual World Series champion.

That means there is no guaranteed 2026 dollar figure for reaching the Wild Card Series, Division Series, League Championship Series or World Series before the postseason is complete.

Gate receipts and the way each team divides its allocation ultimately determine what an individual player receives. Recent years, however, show just how large those rewards can become.

How the MLB postseason bonus pool works

The World Series winner receives 36% of the overall players’ pool, giving the champion by far the largest share of the postseason money.

The losing World Series team receives 24%, while the two clubs eliminated in the League Championship Series split another 24%. That leaves each LCS loser with 12% of the full pool before its team decides how individual shares will be distributed.

The four Division Series losers divide 13%, while the four teams eliminated in the Wild Card round collectively share the final 3%.

A team then determines how many full shares, partial shares and cash awards it will hand out to players, coaches and other staff. That voting process is why two players eliminated at the same stage can end up receiving different postseason checks depending on their club.

Recent payout figures illustrate the scale of the difference. When the Dodgers won the World Series in 2025, a full share was worth more than $484,000, while players on the losing World Series team received full shares worth more than $354,000.

What players could make during MLB 2026 playoffs

Those numbers drop sharply once teams are eliminated before the World Series .

Full shares for clubs knocked out in the 2025 League Championship Series were worth roughly $169,000 to $182,000. Division Series losers generally received around $46,000 to $52,000 per full share, while Wild Card exits produced full shares in the neighborhood of $9,000 to $11,500.

The difference is significant, particularly for players earning closer to the major-league minimum rather than superstar salaries. A World Series run can turn an October bonus into the equivalent of several months of regular-season pay for some members of a roster.

The overall pool has also grown considerably in recent years. The 2024 postseason created a record $129.1 million fund, fueled by strong gate receipts and a World Series between the Yankees and Dodgers .

That record showed how much the teams involved, ticket demand and postseason attendance can influence the final payout. The 2026 figures won't be known until the postseason has ended and every club has finalized its distribution plan.

What is already clear is that each additional round carries a substantial financial reward. A player whose team survives from the Wild Card round all the way to a World Series title can finish October with hundreds of thousands of dollars more than someone eliminated at the first hurdle.

The championship ring remains the prize everyone wants. The postseason check is a valuable reminder that winning in October pays in more ways than one.

articles.title: Boston Red Sox - New York Yankees: What time is the Wild Card Series games and where to watch it
articles.standfirst: Yankees and Red Sox revive baseball's hottest rivalry in the Bronx postseason
articles.summary: Yankees and Red Sox revive baseball's hottest rivalry in the Bronx postseason
articles.body:
There are rivalries, and then there's Yankees–Red Sox. Baseball's oldest and fiercest returns when it matters most: in October, with a ticket to the next round on the line. New York hosts Boston at Yankee Stadium in the Major League postseason, and this time the stage is a short series that forgives no mistakes.

The Mules finished the regular season above the Red Sox, but in October the pecking order of the schedule matters less than a good left-handed pitcher and a timely home run.

Boston Red Sox - New York Yankees: The Wild Card Series setting

The Yankees finished the year in second place in the American League East with a 93-68 record, while the Red Sox came in third with a mark of 87-75. The six-game difference in the regular season suggests a slight advantage for the home team, but the gap narrows in a single-elimination format.

Just remember that New York allowed only 601 runs during the year—the stingiest pitching staff in the entire American League—a statistic that is usually worth its weight in gold in October. Boston, for its part, was not far behind on the mound: 611 runs allowed, the second-best mark in the American League.

Two solid rotations, two bullpens with experienced arms, and a rivalry that guarantees tension from the very first pitch.

Full series schedule and where to watch the Red Sox - Yankees games

The series is played entirely in the Bronx, with Yankee Stadium (capacity 47,309) serving as the venue for the three scheduled games:

Yankees vs Red Sox Game 1

Date: Tuesday, September 29, 2026

Yankees vs Red Sox Game 2

Date: Wednesday, September 30, 2026

Yankees vs Red Sox Game 3 *

Date: Thursday, October 1, 2026

Regarding the broadcast of each game in the series, the Major League postseason is divided among the largest networks, in addition to regional ones in local markets and MLB.tv for out-of-market games. For this particular series, the games can be watched as follows:

Streaming: DIRECTV, fubo and Peacock

The all-out showdown in the Boston Red Sox - New York Yankees

What makes this matchup special is the depth of arms on both sides. The Yankees built their season around a rotation led by Max Fried, the 32-year-old left-hander, and Gerrit Cole, the 36-year-old veteran who remains the staff's benchmark.

Behind them are Carlos Rodón and the young Cam Schlittler, just 25 years old, on a roster that combines experience and fresh blood. In the bullpen, names like David Bednar and Puerto Rican Fernando Cruz bring experience to close out tight innings.

Boston answers with one of the most feared rotations of the year. Garrett Crochet, a 27-year-old left-hander, is the ace of the project, backed by Sonny Gray, the 36-year-old veteran, and Venezuelan Ranger Suárez.

The surprise came from rookie Payton Tolle, 23, who earned a spot in the rotation. And in the closing role appears a familiar face from the Bronx: Cuban Aroldis Chapman, 38, now wearing the Red Sox uniform, ready to put out fires in the final innings.

At the plate, catcher Austin Wells leads New York's offense, while Boston boasts a luxury duo behind home plate with Adley Rutschman and Connor Wong. The battle to control the pace of the game—which pitcher commands the count, which catcher handles his staff better—could define each matchup.

What is the forecast for the game between the Yankees and Red Sox?

The market sees the Yankees as favorites in this second game, with an implied probability of 57.8% compared to the Red Sox's 42.2%. The run line places New York at -1.5 and Boston at +1.5, while the total stands at 6.5 runs, a low number that reflects the respect both pitching staffs command. Everything points to a game with few hits and razor-thin decisions.

The home-field advantage and the depth of New York's staff tip the scales toward the Yankees, but in a short series against Boston, nothing is written in stone. Prediction: New York edges out this game, 4-3, in a matchup decided in the final innings.

articles.title: This Red Sox star feels “like sh*t” while the Yankees celebrate big win with champagne
articles.standfirst: Garrett Crochet and Willson Contreras were left questioning how Boston’s season ended
articles.summary: Garrett Crochet and Willson Contreras were left questioning how Boston’s season ended
articles.body:
The final out had barely settled before the contrast became impossible to miss.

New York was celebrating a two-game wild-card sweep of the Red Sox , champagne flowing as players prepared for an ALDS matchup with Tampa Bay. Boston, meanwhile, was left to digest another postseason exit at the hands of its biggest rival.

Garrett Crochet captured the frustration better than anyone.

“I feel healthy but I feel like s**t,” Crochet said after the loss.

The left-hander had returned to the mound for the first time since late April following a battle with left shoulder inflammation, but his comeback lasted only four batters. Crochet allowed three runs on four hits without recording an out.

Yankees turn rivalry into another celebration

New York dominated the series from start to finish, outscoring Boston 18-2 across two games and giving the Red Sox little room to respond.

Cody Bellinger delivered the decisive blow in Game 2, launching a three-run homer in the sixth inning that effectively ended Boston’s hopes of extending the series.

“Honestly, this place is such an amazing place to play in the postseason,” Bellinger told YES Network. “Fans are so into the game; it’s just an electric atmosphere. It’s really special.”

Aaron Judge did not play because of a right calf strain, but he was still part of the clubhouse celebration afterward.

“We’re definitely inspired by the Knicks, gotta keep the winning going in New York,” Judge said.

The Yankees now move on with momentum. The Red Sox leave with questions.

Crochet was not the only player struggling to process the loss.

Willson Contreras, one of Boston’s few productive hitters in Game 2, went 2-for-2 with a home run and two walks. The rest of the lineup combined for just two hits.

Asked why the offense had fallen so sharply after a strong stretch earlier in the season, Contreras initially held back.

“That’s a good question. I’m not going to answer it because I don’t want to give my honest answer,” he said. “We got eliminated. That’s the bottom line.”

He later pointed to what he believes is an overreliance on data.

“It’s not enough when you have talent or you have data or you have computers telling you what to do,” Contreras said. “This is baseball and the data is here to help us. But at the end of the day, you’re going to need experience and veteran guys to win games.”

Asked directly whether Boston had leaned too heavily on analytics, Contreras replied: “If you watch the game. If you watch the game.”

The Yankees leave the series with another postseason victory over Boston and a champagne-soaked clubhouse.

The Red Sox leave with another early playoff exit and an offseason that now begins with frustration instead of momentum.

Yankees turn rivalry into another celebration
New York dominated the series from start to finish, outscoring Boston 18-2 across two games and giving the Red Sox little room to respond.
Cody Bellinger delivered the decisive blow in Game 2, launching a three-run homer in the sixth inning that effectively ended Boston’s hopes of extending the series.
“Honestly, this place is such an amazing place to play in the postseason,” Bellinger told YES Network. “Fans are so into the game; it’s just an electric atmosphere. It’s really special.”
Aaron Judge did not play because of a right calf strain, but he was still part of the clubhouse celebration afterward.
“We’re definitely inspired by the Knicks, gotta keep the winning going in New York,” Judge said.
The Yankees now move on with momentum. The Red Sox leave with questions.
Crochet was not the only player struggling to process the loss.
Willson Contreras, one of Boston’s few productive hitters in Game 2, went 2-for-2 with a home run and two walks. The rest of the lineup combined for just two hits.
Asked why the offense had fallen so sharply after a strong stretch earlier in the season, Contreras initially held back.
“That’s a good question. I’m not going to answer it because I don’t want to give my honest answer,” he said. “We got eliminated. That’s the bottom line.”
He later pointed to what he believes is an overreliance on data.

“It’s not enough when you have talent or you have data or you have computers telling you what to do,” Contreras said. “This is baseball and the data is here to help us. But at the end of the day, you’re going to need experience and veteran guys to win games.”
Asked directly whether Boston had leaned too heavily on analytics, Contreras replied: “If you watch the game. If you watch the game.”
The Yankees leave the series with another postseason victory over Boston and a champagne-soaked clubhouse.
The Red Sox leave with another early playoff exit and an offseason that now begins with frustration instead of momentum.
